title: Taiwan Semiconductor Gives Gloomy Outlook on Smartphone Demand - Barron's

https://www.barrons.com/articles/taiwan-semiconductor-gives-gloomy-outlook-on-smartphone-demand-51547738801 Taiwan Semiconductor Gives Gloomy Outlook on Smartphone Demand By Jan. 17, 2019 10:26 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Sam Yeh/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) sparked worries about the severity of the chip industry downturn after it gave guidance on Thursday significantly below the Wall Street consensus.
The company reported December-quarter sales of $9.4 billion, slightly above the Wall Street consensus of $9.37 billion. But it also gave a March-quarter revenue guidance range of $7.3 billion to $7.4 billion—versus the $8 billion average analyst estimate.
TSMC is the world’s largest semiconductor foundry company and manufactures chips for companies such as Apple (AAPL), Nvidia (NVDA), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). Due to its large size, the company’s results are widely regarded as proxy for global chip demand.
Read more: Apple Watchers Are Already Looking Toward the Next Next iPhones
“Moving into first quarter 2019, we anticipate our business will be dampened by the overall weakening of the macroeconomic outlook, mobile product seasonality, and high levels of inventory in the semiconductor supply chain,” Lora Ho , chief financial officer of TSMC, was quoted in the earnings release.
The Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing American depositary receipt, which trades on the NYSE, was down 0.4% in early trading on Thursday, to $35.49.
On its conference call, the company said it would take “a couple of quarters” for the semiconductor supply chain to digest its excess inventory. Management cited high-end smartphone demand and cryptocurrency mining as key areas of weakness.
The company added due to the weaker macroeconomic outlook, it has lowered its 2019 capital expenditure forecast range to $10 billion to $11 billion, down from its normal long-term budget of $10 billion to $12 billion.
Susquehanna Financial Group analyst Mehdi Hosseini said in a note to clients TSMC’s guidance suggests chip demand from corporate data centers is deteriorating. He added the tone from the company seems to be “more cautious.”
Stock prices of many chip makers traded lowered on Thursday. AMD, Skyworks Solutions (SWKS), and Analog Devices (ADI) shares all declined in early trading.
